review.title: False imprisonment defined
review.plain: False imprisonment is the unlawful violation of the personal liberty of another; the section sets no punishment itself.
acts: the unlawful violation of the personal liberty of another

crimes.act: Violates the personal liberty of another

penalties.penalty: Set in Section 237

review.title: Human trafficking
review.plain: Depriving or violating another person's liberty to obtain forced labor or services, or to commit certain listed offenses, or inducing a minor into a commercial sex act, is human trafficking punishable by up to life in state prison.
acts: deprives or violates the personal liberty of another
causes, induces, or persuades, or attempts to cause, induce, or persuade, a person who is a minor at the time of commission of the offense to engage in a commercial sex act

terms: "Commercial sex act": sexual conduct on account of which anything of value is given or received by a person
"Minor": a person less than 18 years of age

"Forced labor or services": labor or services that are performed or provided by a person and are obtained or maintained through force, fraud, duress, or coercion, or equivalent conduct that would reasonably overbear the will of the person

"Deprivation or violation of the personal liberty of another": includes substantial and sustained restriction of another's liberty accomplished through force, fear, fraud, deceit, coercion, violence, duress, menace, or threat of unlawful injury to the victim or to another person, under circumstances where the person receiving or apprehending the threat reasonably believes that it is likely that the person making the threat would carry it out
consequences: Consent by a victim who is a minor at the time of the offense is not a defense
Mistake of fact as to the age of a victim who is a minor at the time of the offense is not a defense
A court shall report a conviction of subdivision (a), (b), or (c) that occurred while the person was using a commercial motor vehicle to the Department of Motor Vehicles

crimes.act: Deprives or violates the personal liberty of another

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in the state prison for 5, 8, or 12 years and a fine of not more than five hundred thousand dollars ($500,000)

intent: With the intent to obtain forced labor or services

crimes.act: Deprives or violates the personal liberty of another

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in the state prison for 8, 14, or 20 years and a fine of not more than five hundred thousand dollars ($500,000)

intent: With the intent to effect or maintain a violation of Section 266, 266h, 266i, 266j, 267, 311.1, 311.2, 311.3, 311.4, 311.5, 311.6, or 518

crimes.act: Causes, induces, or persuades, or attempts to cause, induce, or persuade, a person who is a minor at the time of commission of the offense to engage in a commercial sex act
ways: attempts to cause, induce, or persuade
conditions: The person caused, induced, or persuaded is a minor at the time of commission of the offense

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in the state prison for 5, 8, or 12 years and a fine of not more than five hundred thousand dollars ($500,000)

penalties.if: the offense involves force, fear, fraud, deceit, coercion, violence, duress, menace, or threat of unlawful injury to the victim or to another person
penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in the state prison for 15 years to life and a fine of not more than five hundred thousand dollars ($500,000)

intent: With the intent to effect or maintain a violation of Section 266, 266h, 266i, 266j, 267, 311.1, 311.2, 311.3, 311.4, 311.5, 311.6, or 518

review.title: Human trafficking victim indicators
review.plain: Requires law enforcement to use due diligence to identify human trafficking victims and to consider listed indicators of trafficking.

review.title: Victim interview rights
review.plain: Gives human trafficking victims the right to an advocate and support person at interviews and requires they be told of that right.

review.title: Human trafficking victim defense
review.plain: Creates an affirmative defense for a person coerced to commit an offense as a direct result of being a trafficking victim, and sets the relief if it succeeds.

review.title: Partner violence coercion defense
review.plain: Creates an affirmative defense for a person coerced to commit an offense as a direct result of intimate partner or sexual violence, and sets the relief if it succeeds.

review.title: Nuisance procedures after trafficking
review.plain: Applies public nuisance procedures and remedies to real property used to facilitate human trafficking after a conviction.

review.title: Human trafficking enhancements
review.plain: Great bodily injury during human trafficking adds a consecutive 5, 7, or 10 years in state prison, and a prior trafficking conviction adds a consecutive 5 years for each; the court may also add a fine up to $1,000,000.
acts: inflicts great bodily injury on a victim in the commission or attempted commission of a violation of Section 236.1
has previously been convicted of a violation of any crime specified in Section 236.1

consequences: Upon conviction of a violation of Section 236.1, the court may, in addition to any other penalty, fine, or restitution, order the defendant to pay an additional fine not to exceed one million dollars ($1,000,000)
Fines are deposited in the Victim-Witness Assistance Fund

crimes.act: Inflicts great bodily injury on a victim in the commission or attempted commission of a violation of Section 236.1
conditions: Great bodily injury is inflicted on a victim in the commission or attempted commission of a violation of Section 236.1

penalties.penalty: An additional and consecutive term of imprisonment in the state prison for 5, 7, or 10 years

crimes.act: Has previously been convicted of a violation of any crime specified in Section 236.1
conditions: The person has previously been convicted of a violation of any crime specified in Section 236.1
Each additional conviction was on charges separately brought and tried

penalties.penalty: An additional and consecutive term of imprisonment in the state prison for 5 years for each additional conviction on charges separately brought and tried

review.title: Law enforcement endorsement letters
review.plain: Requires law enforcement to provide endorsement letters for human trafficking victims and sets rules for submitting and denying them.

review.title: Asset preservation proceedings
review.plain: Lets prosecutors petition for orders preserving assets of a person charged with human trafficking, and sets notice, claim, and hearing procedures.

review.title: Forfeiture for trafficking of minors
review.plain: Allows forfeiture of property used in or gained from human trafficking involving a commercial sex act with a minor, with limits for certain property.

review.title: Forfeiture petition procedure
review.plain: Sets the petition and notice procedure for forfeiture in trafficking cases involving a commercial sex act with a minor.

review.title: Forfeiture claims and hearing
review.plain: Sets how interested persons file claims and how the forfeiture hearing proceeds, including the burden of proof.

review.title: Orders to preserve forfeitable property
review.plain: Lets the court issue orders pending forfeiture to preserve property, including injunctions and receivers.

review.title: Forfeiture orders and liens
review.plain: Sets the court's orders on forfeited property and how lienholders are treated.

review.title: Distribution of forfeited property
review.plain: Sets how forfeited money and sale proceeds are distributed.

review.title: Victim Witness help for minors
review.plain: Requires that a minor trafficking victim be given Victim Witness Assistance Center help if the minor wishes.

review.title: Vacatur for trafficking victims
review.plain: Lets a trafficking victim petition to vacate convictions, arrests, and adjudications for nonviolent offenses committed as a victim, and sets the procedure.

review.title: Vacatur for partner violence victims
review.plain: Lets a victim of intimate partner or sexual violence petition to vacate convictions for nonviolent offenses committed as a victim, and sets the procedure.

review.title: False imprisonment punishment
review.plain: False imprisonment is punishable by a fine up to $1,000 or up to one year in county jail, and by imprisonment under subdivision (h) of Section 1170 if done by violence, menace, fraud, or deceit.
acts: False imprisonment
False imprisonment of an elder or dependent adult by use of violence, menace, fraud, or deceit

crimes.act: Commits false imprisonment

penalties.penalty: A fine not exceeding one thousand dollars ($1,000), or imprisonment in the county jail for not more than one year, or both that fine and imprisonment

penalties.if: the false imprisonment is effected by violence, menace, fraud, or deceit
penalties.penalty: Imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170

crimes.act: Commits false imprisonment of an elder or dependent adult by use of violence, menace, fraud, or deceit
conditions: The victim is an elder or dependent adult
The false imprisonment is by use of violence, menace, fraud, or deceit

penalties.penalty: Punishable as described in subdivision (f) of Section 368. Set in Section 368

review.title: Assault defined
review.plain: An assault is an unlawful attempt, coupled with a present ability, to commit a violent injury on another person; the section sets no punishment itself.
acts: an unlawful attempt, coupled with a present ability, to commit a violent injury on the person of another

crimes.act: Makes an unlawful attempt, coupled with a present ability, to commit a violent injury on the person of another
conditions: The person has a present ability to commit the violent injury

penalties.penalty: Set in Section 241

review.title: Assault punishment
review.plain: Assault is punishable by a fine up to $1,000 or up to six months in county jail, with higher fines and up to one year in jail when committed against certain officers and workers.
acts: assault
an assault is committed against the person of a parking control officer engaged in the performance of their duties

an assault is committed against the person of a peace officer, firefighter, emergency medical technician, lifeguard, process server, traffic officer, code enforcement officer, animal control officer, or search and rescue member engaged in the performance of their duties

terms: "Parking control officer": any person employed by a city, county, or city and county, to monitor and enforce state laws and local ordinances relating to parking
"Traffic officer": any person employed by a county or city to monitor and enforce state laws and local ordinances relating to parking and the operation of vehicles
"Animal control officer": any person employed by a county or city for purposes of enforcing animal control laws or regulations
"Search and rescue member": any person who is part of an organized search and rescue team managed by a governmental agency

"Health care worker": a person who, in the course and scope of employment, performs duties directly associated with the care and treatment rendered by the hospital's emergency department or the department's security

crimes.act: Commits an assault

penalties.penalty: A fine not exceeding one thousand dollars ($1,000), or imprisonment in the county jail not exceeding six months, or both the fine and imprisonment

crimes.act: Commits an assault against the person of a parking control officer engaged in the performance of their duties
conditions: The victim is a parking control officer engaged in the performance of their duties

penalties.penalty: A fine not exceeding two thousand dollars ($2,000), or imprisonment in the county jail not exceeding six months, or both the fine and imprisonment

knowledge: Knowing or reasonably should know that the victim is a parking control officer

crimes.act: Commits an assault against the person of a peace officer, firefighter, emergency medical technician, lifeguard, process server, traffic officer, code enforcement officer, animal control officer, or search and rescue member engaged in the performance of their duties, or a physician or nurse engaged in rendering emergency medical care outside a hospital, clinic, or other health care facility, or a physician, nurse, or other health care worker of a hospital engaged in providing services within the emergency department
conditions: The victim is a peace officer, firefighter, emergency medical technician, lifeguard, process server, traffic officer, code enforcement officer, animal control officer, or search and rescue member engaged in the performance of their duties, or a physician or nurse engaged in rendering emergency medical care outside a hospital, clinic, or other health care facility, or a physician, nurse, or other health care worker of a hospital engaged in providing services within the emergency department

penalties.penalty: A fine not exceeding two thousand dollars ($2,000), or imprisonment in a county jail not exceeding one year, or both the fine and imprisonment

knowledge: Knowing or reasonably should know that the victim is in one of the listed categories and engaged in the performance of the listed duties

review.title: Assault on custodial officer
review.plain: Assault on a custodial officer is punishable by up to one year in county jail or by imprisonment under subdivision (h) of Section 1170.
acts: an assault is committed against the person of a custodial officer as defined in Section 831 or 831.5

crimes.act: Commits an assault against the person of a custodial officer as defined in Section 831 or 831.5
conditions: The victim is a custodial officer engaged in the performance of his or her duties

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in the county jail not exceeding one year, or imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170

knowledge: Knowing or reasonably should know that the victim is a custodial officer engaged in the performance of his or her duties

review.title: Assault on school or park property
review.plain: Assault on school or park property is punishable by a fine up to $2,000 or up to one year in county jail, or both.
acts: an assault is committed on school or park property against any person

terms: "School": any elementary school, junior high school, four-year high school, senior high school, adult school or any branch thereof, opportunity school, continuation high school, regional occupational center, evening high school, technical school, or community college
"Park": any publicly maintained or operated park, not including any facility when used for professional sports or commercial events

crimes.act: Commits an assault on school or park property against any person
conditions: The assault is committed on school or park property

penalties.penalty: A fine not exceeding two thousand dollars ($2,000), or imprisonment in the county jail not exceeding one year, or both that fine and imprisonment

consequences: When committed by a minor on school property, the court may order the minor to attend counseling at the expense of the minor's parents, in addition to any other fine or sentence or as a condition of probation

review.title: Assault on public transportation
review.plain: Assault on any person on the property of, or a motor vehicle of, a public transportation provider is punishable by a fine up to $2,000 or up to one year in county jail, or both.
acts: an assault is committed against any person on the property of, or on a motor vehicle of, a public transportation provider

terms: "Public transportation provider": a publicly or privately owned entity that operates, for the transportation of persons for hire, a bus, taxicab, streetcar, cable car, trackless trolley, or other motor vehicle, including a vehicle operated on stationary rails or on a track or rail suspended in air, or that operates a schoolbus
"On the property of": the entire station where public transportation is available, including the parking lot reserved for the public who utilize the transportation system

crimes.act: Commits an assault against any person on the property of, or on a motor vehicle of, a public transportation provider
conditions: The assault is against a person on the property of, or on a motor vehicle of, a public transportation provider

penalties.penalty: A fine not to exceed two thousand dollars ($2,000), or imprisonment in a county jail not to exceed one year, or both the fine and imprisonment

review.title: Assault on school police officer
review.plain: Assault is punishable by a fine up to $1,000 or up to six months in county jail; against a school district police officer it is punishable by up to one year in county jail or under subdivision (h) of Section 1170.
acts: An assault is punishable

the assault is committed against the person of a peace officer engaged in the performance of his or her duties as a member of a police department of a school district pursuant to Section 38000 of the Education Code

crimes.act: Commits an assault

penalties.penalty: A fine not exceeding one thousand dollars ($1,000), or imprisonment in the county jail not exceeding six months, or both

crimes.act: Commits an assault against the person of a peace officer engaged in the performance of his or her duties as a member of a police department of a school district pursuant to Section 38000 of the Education Code
conditions: The victim is a peace officer engaged in the performance of his or her duties as a member of a police department of a school district pursuant to Section 38000 of the Education Code

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in the county jail not exceeding one year, or imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170

knowledge: Knowing or reasonably should know that the victim is a peace officer engaged in the performance of his or her duties

review.title: Assault on highway worker
review.plain: Assault on a highway worker engaged in their duties is punishable by a fine up to $2,000 or up to one year in county jail, or both.
acts: an assault is committed against a highway worker engaged in the performance of his or her duties

terms: "Highway worker": an employee of the Department of Transportation, a contractor or employee of a contractor while working under contract with the Department of Transportation, an employee of a city, county, or city and county, a contractor or employee of a contractor while working under contract with a city, county, or city and county, or a volunteer as defined in Section 1720.4 of the Labor Code who performs maintenance, repair, or construction, operates equipment, or performs related maintenance work on state highway or local street or road infrastructures in work zones

crimes.act: Commits an assault against a highway worker engaged in the performance of his or her duties
conditions: The victim is a highway worker engaged in the performance of his or her duties

penalties.penalty: A fine not to exceed two thousand dollars ($2,000) or imprisonment in a county jail up to one year or both that fine and imprisonment

knowledge: Knowing or reasonably should know that the victim is a highway worker engaged in the performance of his or her duties

review.title: Assault on school employee
review.plain: Assault on a school employee engaged in their duties or in retaliation for their duties is punishable by up to one year in county jail, a fine up to $2,000, or both.
acts: an assault is committed against a school employee engaged in the performance of his or her duties, or in retaliation for an act performed in the course of his or her duties

terms: "School employee": has the same meaning as defined in subdivision (d) of Section 245.5

crimes.act: Commits an assault against a school employee engaged in the performance of his or her duties, or in retaliation for an act performed in the course of his or her duties
conditions: The victim is a school employee engaged in the performance of his or her duties, or the assault is in retaliation for an act performed in the course of his or her duties, whether on or off campus, during the schoolday or at any other time
exceptions: Conduct arising during the course of an otherwise lawful labor dispute

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in a county jail not exceeding one year, or a fine not exceeding two thousand dollars ($2,000), or both the fine and imprisonment

knowledge: Knowing or reasonably should know the victim is a school employee

review.title: Assault on juror
review.plain: A party to a jury case who assaults a juror or alternate juror during or after the case is punishable by a fine up to $2,000, up to one year in county jail, or imprisonment under subdivision (h) of Section 1170.
acts: commits an assault against any juror or alternate juror who was selected and sworn in that legal action

crimes.act: Commits an assault against any juror or alternate juror who was selected and sworn in that legal action
conditions: The assault is committed while the legal action is pending or after the conclusion of the trial
The victim is a juror or alternate juror who was selected and sworn in that legal action

penalties.penalty: A fine not to exceed two thousand dollars ($2,000), or imprisonment in the county jail not exceeding one year, or both such fine and imprisonment, or imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170

crimes.who: A party to a civil or criminal action in which a jury has been selected to try the case

review.title: Assault on armed forces member
review.plain: Assault on a member of the United States Armed Forces because of the victim's service is punishable by a fine up to $2,000, up to one year in county jail, or both.
acts: commits an assault against a member of the United States Armed Forces

terms: "Because of": the bias motivation must be a cause in fact of the assault, whether or not other causes exist; when multiple concurrent motives exist, the prohibited bias must be a substantial factor in bringing about the assault

crimes.act: Commits an assault against a member of the United States Armed Forces
conditions: The assault is because of the victim's service in the United States Armed Forces

penalties.penalty: A fine not exceeding two thousand dollars ($2,000), by imprisonment in a county jail for a period not exceeding one year, or by both that fine and imprisonment
